title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The headline states that a Minnesota lawyer was suspended in connection with fake AI case citations, but the underlying article text was not captured, so the specific facts of the case, including which AI system was used, how many citations were fabricated, and the precise terms of the suspension, are not established from the available sourcing.

What the headline does indicate is a failure mode that has appeared in other documented incidents: a generative AI system producing plausible-looking but nonexistent legal citations, which a lawyer then submitted to a court without independently verifying their existence. This failure occurs at the point of human use, where a professional relies on AI output as if it were a reliable retrieval system rather than a text generator that can assert false information as fact. A basic check, confirming each cited case against an authoritative legal database before filing, would have been sufficient to catch the error before it reached the court.

Whether the submission was intentional misrepresentation or negligent reliance on the AI is not established by the available reporting.
